The MIT of Sake Education- SUPERB!
Sep 2019
I am US based but in Vietnam almost monthly for business. As an enthusiastic but unsophisticated sake aficionado, I booked a table right away after hearing about this relatively new restaurant from my hotel's management. When I got there, I realized that I'd been to the tiny 2nd story location before, when it was a weird little bar in the heart of Saigon's District 1. 

Having seen the location before, the architectural transformation of what is a very small and unusual floor plan was nothing less than amazing. The tiny stairwell which leads you from the street level entry door to the restaurant has been converted from a creepy winding hallway into a dark, soothing, and inviting start to your sake adventure. It reminded me of the stunning Aronia de Takazawa in Tokyo, one of my top 2 favorite restaurants on the planet: in each case, an elusive, unassuming street entrance turns into a intriguing prequel of the amazing experience which lies just up the staircase.

Once inside Sake Central, I immediately appreciated the time, thought, and effort it must have taken to convert the small area into what is a stunningly beautiful room which is inviting, intimate, yet comfortable. The large communal table set up maximizes capacity for the owners, but somehow does so effortlessly. I am not a big fan of shared tables but here, it was not an issue...it just works.

The sake selection: SUPERB and better than any I’ve found in this part of the world (outside of Japan, obviously). As I've said, I'm no expert but I know what I like and with sake, it’s a love/hate thing: I am passionate about certain styles while others - solid, award-winning varieties - taste absolutely undrinkable to me. I explained that to Thanh, our server, and he immediately launched into his recommendations based on my preferences. Thanh was simply FANTASTIC in going over the sake list in detail with me; I was there for an early dinner so it wasn't crowded, and I'd say he spent more than a half hour explaining and elaborating as I peppered him with endless questions (while my poor dining companion suffered through my Sake Nerd Session patiently LOL). I tried 3, all were spot on recommendations. Later, I was given the gift of a small paper handbook prepared by Sake Central’s owners. (I didn’t open it till this morning; what I expected to be a promotional booklet is actually a wonderfully written, succinct crash course on Sake, complete with a section for tasting notes on the back. A keeper for sure.)

Food: we opted against the Omikase dinner combination and instead went a la carte with appetizers. The food was excellent, small sharing portions, delivered one at a time to maximize the experience. I can’t remember the name of the Japanese oysters of the day, but they were HUGE, fresh, and delicious, served on ice with a kumquat mignonette. Sadly, they were out of the raw Yellowfin tuna appetizer, but the other big standout was double-miso Black Cod...superb. Every bit as perfect as Joel Robuchon’s legendary “Le Black Cod”. Really.

I asked about ownership and Thanh mentioned there were multiple partners; in the booklet, I saw the Pizza 4ps is involved. Pizza 4ps has the absolute best pizza in this part of the world and, best of all, they make their own artisan cheeses. One of the events they have is a sake/home made cheese pairing...VERY original and VERY cool.

My two constructive suggestions to Sake Central’s otherwise masterful execution are the following: first of all, create several sake flights which let someone like me experience 6-7 small tastings at one time. All three of the sakes I had were excellent, and one was a very expensive rare brand. I would have liked to have tasted more. Second – and for all I know they may be already doing this – is create once or twice a week themed events (like their sake + cheese night) on their slow nights to fill the restaurant and create a recurring crowd of fans. Their concept is unique in this amazing food city and news will spread quickly. In a few weeks, tables will be pre-booked a week in advance, I’m certain. Thanh is perfectly capable of leading the shared table to understand each progressive sake step in the flight and the young chef who delivered the Miso Cod was equally eloquent and enthusiastic.

Sake Central is just a lovely place, the product of much thinking, serious expertise, and passionate execution. It shows in the way the place is built, in the sake selection, in the execution of the food and, as a restaurant owner myself, most importantly in the way its young staff has been not only trained but EDUCATED on the beautiful nuances of sake culture. I’ll be back every time!
